nodes.summary: The lossy one-place acknowledgement channel of the lossy go-back-N variant, given by its transitions in each state. When empty, it inputs on $\mathsf{reply}_k$ and then holds $k$, for each $k \in \{0, 1, 2\}$. When it holds $k$, it either outputs on $\mathsf{ack}_k$ or silently loses $k$, and in both cases it becomes empty. It has no other transitions.
nodes.title: Transitions of the lossy acknowledgement channel

nodes.summary: For a go-back-N sender with window base $b$, $c$ outstanding messages and next-frame offset $o$, and an acknowledgement $k$, let $d = \max(k + 3 - b, 0) \bmod 3$. If $1 \le d \le c$, the window slides: the new sender has base $k$, $c - d$ outstanding messages and next-frame offset $\max(o - d, 0)$. Otherwise the sender is unchanged.
nodes.title: Sender update on an acknowledgement

nodes.summary: The two-place buffer process of the go-back-N model with occupancy $0$.
nodes.title: The empty two-place buffer

nodes.summary: For every occupancy $n$, every process reachable from the go-back-N buffer with occupancy $n$ by zero or more silent steps is that buffer itself.
nodes.title: The silent closure of the buffer is trivial

nodes.summary: The transitions of the go-back-N two-place buffer at occupancy $n \in \mathbb{N}$: if $n < 2$ it inputs on $\mathsf{acc}$ and moves to occupancy $n + 1$, and if $n > 0$ it outputs on $\mathsf{del}$ and moves to occupancy $n - 1$. It has no other transitions.
nodes.title: Transitions of the two-place buffer

nodes.summary: For every occupancy $n$ and every visible label $a$, if the go-back-N buffer with occupancy $n$ reaches a process $Q$ by a weak transition labelled $a$ (silent steps, one $a$-step, silent steps), then $Q$ is the buffer with some occupancy $m$ such that the buffer at occupancy $n$ has a transition labelled $a$ to occupancy $m$.
nodes.title: Visible weak steps of the buffer

nodes.summary: For an occupancy $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the process constant of the go-back-N specification for the two-place buffer holding $n$ messages.
nodes.title: The two-place buffer process

nodes.summary: A list of $147$ pairs, each a go-back-N configuration together with the occupancy of the two-place buffer it simulates, namely the number of accepted but undelivered messages. It contains every reachable configuration, and it is ordered so that every pair can reach the visible actions of its buffer state through pairs listed earlier.
nodes.title: Weak-bisimulation certificate for go-back-N

nodes.summary: The transitions of a go-back-N configuration (sender, data channel, receiver) are those of the parallel composition of the three components, in which one component moves alone or two components synchronize on complementary labels in a silent step, restricted to the silent steps and the steps whose label is not on an internal channel ($\mathsf{send}_k$, $\mathsf{recv}_k$ or $\mathsf{ack}_k$ for $k \in \{0, 1, 2\}$).
nodes.title: Transitions of go-back-N configurations

nodes.summary: A configuration of the go-back-N protocol consists of a sender state, the content of the data channel (either empty or a single frame with sequence number $k \in \mathbb{N}$), and a receiver state.
nodes.title: Go-back-N configurations

nodes.summary: The data channel holds at most one frame. When empty, for each sequence number $k \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ it can input on channel $\mathrm{send}_k$ and then hold frame $k$. When holding frame $k$, it can either output on channel $\mathrm{recv}_k$ or silently lose the frame by a $\tau$ step; in both cases it becomes empty.
nodes.title: Transitions of the go-back-N data channel

nodes.summary: The go-back-N protocol is observation congruent (rooted weakly bisimilar) to the empty two-place buffer: every transition of either process is matched by a rooted weak transition of the other with the same label (silent steps, a step with that label, silent steps), and the resulting processes are weakly bisimilar.
nodes.title: Go-back-N with window 2 is observation congruent to a two-place buffer

nodes.summary: Over a lossy one-place data channel, with timeouts and cumulative acknowledgements, the protocol is weakly bisimilar to the empty two-place buffer.
nodes.title: Go-back-N with window 2 implements a two-place buffer

nodes.summary: The go-back-N protocol with window size $2$ and sequence numbers modulo $3$ is the recursive CCS process in its initial configuration: the parallel composition of the sender with an empty window based at $0$, the empty lossy one-place data channel, and the receiver expecting $0$, with the internal channels $\mathrm{send}_k$, $\mathrm{recv}_k$ and $\mathrm{ack}_k$ for $k \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ restricted.
nodes.title: The go-back-N protocol

nodes.summary: The initial configuration of the go-back-N protocol consists of the sender with window base $0$, no outstanding messages and next-frame offset $0$; the empty data channel; and the receiver expecting sequence number $0$.
nodes.title: Initial configuration of go-back-N

nodes.summary: The internal channels of the go-back-N protocol are $\mathrm{send}_k$ (sender to data channel), $\mathrm{recv}_k$ (data channel to receiver) and $\mathrm{ack}_k$ (receiver to sender) for $k \in \{0, 1, 2\}$; all of them are restricted.
nodes.title: Internal channels of go-back-N

nodes.summary: The transitions of a configuration of the lossy go-back-N variant come from the parallel composition of the sender, the data channel, the lossy-variant receiver and the acknowledgement channel (in each composition either side moves alone, or the two sides synchronize on complementary input and output labels in a silent step), keeping only the silent transitions and those whose label is not on an internal channel…
nodes.title: Transitions of lossy go-back-N configurations

nodes.summary: A configuration of the lossy go-back-N variant is a go-back-N configuration (sender state, data channel content, receiver state) together with the content of the acknowledgement channel, either empty or a single acknowledgement $k \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Configurations of lossy go-back-N

nodes.summary: With a lossy acknowledgement channel and the deliver-then-acknowledge receiver, go-back-N is not weakly bisimilar to the two-place buffer. Accept two messages, deliver the first and lose its acknowledgement, and let the receiver take the second frame: the buffer now holds one message and accepts another, but the protocol cannot accept before it delivers.
nodes.title: Lossy acknowledgements break the buffer specification

nodes.summary: The process of the lossy variant of go-back-N in its initial configuration: the sender's window is based at $0$ with no outstanding messages and next offset $0$, the data channel and the acknowledgement channel are empty, and the receiver expects frame $0$.
nodes.title: Go-back-N with a lossy acknowledgement channel

nodes.summary: The list of channels restricted in the lossy variant: the internal channels of the reliable protocol, namely $\mathsf{send}\,k$, $\mathsf{recv}\,k$ and $\mathsf{ack}\,k$ for $k = 0, 1, 2$, followed by the channels $\mathsf{reply}\,0$, $\mathsf{reply}\,1$ and $\mathsf{reply}\,2$ from the receiver to the acknowledgement channel.
nodes.title: Internal channels of lossy go-back-N

nodes.summary: The transitions of the receiver of the lossy variant, as pairs of a label and a successor state, are those of the receiver of the reliable protocol, except in the state about to acknowledge $k$: there the only transition is an output on $\mathsf{reply}\,k$, to the acknowledgement channel, after which the receiver expects $k$.
nodes.title: Receiver transitions of lossy go-back-N

nodes.summary: Let $c$ and $c'$ be configurations of the lossy variant and $a$ a label. If $(a, c')$ is one of the configuration-level transitions of $c$, then in the labelled transition system of the go-back-N specification the lossy process in configuration $c$ has a transition labelled $a$ to the lossy process in configuration $c'$.
nodes.title: Configuration transitions are process transitions in lossy go-back-N

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a configuration of the lossy variant, and let $S$, $D$, $R$ and $A$ be the process constants for its sender state, its data-channel content, its receiver state (as a receiver of the lossy variant) and its acknowledgement-channel content. The process of the lossy variant in $c$ is $((S \mid D) \mid R) \mid A$ with the internal channels of the lossy variant restricted.
nodes.title: The lossy go-back-N process in a configuration

nodes.summary: The labelled transition system whose states are the CCS processes over the go-back-N channel names and process constants, whose labels are the CCS labels over the channel names, and whose transitions are those generated by the go-back-N recursive specification.
nodes.title: Labelled transition system of go-back-N

nodes.summary: The channel names of the go-back-N protocol are $\mathsf{acc}$ (accept a message from the user), $\mathsf{del}$ (deliver a message to the user) and, for every natural number $k$: $\mathsf{send}\,k$ (sender to data channel, a frame with sequence number $k$), $\mathsf{recv}\,k$ (data channel to receiver), $\mathsf{ack}\,k$ (receiver to sender, the cumulative acknowledgement naming $k$ as the next expected frame) and…
nodes.title: Channel names of go-back-N

nodes.summary: The transitions of the receiver, as pairs of a label and a successor state. Expecting $e$, for each $k = 0, 1, 2$ it can input on $\mathsf{recv}\,k$ and then is about to deliver $e$ if $k = e$, and about to acknowledge $e$ otherwise. About to deliver $e$, it outputs on $\mathsf{del}$ and is then about to acknowledge $(e + 1) \bmod 3$. About to acknowledge $k$, it outputs on $\mathsf{ack}\,k$ and then expects $k$.
nodes.title: Receiver transitions of go-back-N

nodes.summary: A receiver state is one of the following, for a natural number $e$ or $k$: expecting the frame with sequence number $e$; about to deliver $e$, having received the expected frame $e$; or about to acknowledge $k$, the next expected sequence number.
nodes.title: Receiver states of go-back-N

nodes.summary: A state of the go-back-N sender is a triple of natural numbers: the base of the window (the sequence number of the oldest unacknowledged frame), the number of outstanding messages (accepted but not yet acknowledged), and the offset from the base of the next frame to transmit.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
